title: Remove a verified manual Windows-authentication downgrade
goal: Let .NET 11 retry a Windows-authenticated HTTP/2 request over HTTP/1.1; use when a tested manual request-version override can be removed while preserving TLS, credentials and strict-version policy.

sdk.reason: Canonical net11.0 consumer; SDK11 RC3 is the exact measured compiler baseline.
sdk.name: .NET SDK

runtime.reason: Automatic Negotiate/NTLM HTTP/2 challenge fallback is implemented by .NET 11 SocketsHttpHandler.
runtime.name: .NET

language.name: C#
language.reason: Canonical net11.0 project explicitly selects C#15.0; the proxy API does not itself require new language syntax. This is the configured example route, not a minimum-language claim.

packageAssets: Request helper uses shared-framework System.Net.Http; Kestrel fixture has exact locked Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.Negotiate and System.DirectoryServices.Protocols 11.0.0-rc.3.26522.148. No backport asserted.
prerequisites: Trusted HTTPS Windows-auth service supporting HTTP/2 and HTTP/1.1; an authorised existing identity.
Use a reused HttpClient with deliberately scoped credentials and normal TLS validation; dispose requests/responses.
platforms: Windows x64 Kestrel/SSPI NTLM with current local Windows identity measured; other platforms and Kerberos not tested.
providers: Windows SSPI and Kestrel Negotiate; no credential/account provisioning or production endpoint.
stabilityLimitations: Actual .NET10.0.14 and .NET11 RC3 evidence; final GA remains PIN-962 and PIN-959 work.
constraints: Strict HTTP/2 does not downgrade. Automatic retry does not grant credentials or authorisation.
Retain the manual HTTP/1.1 route on .NET 10; no global HTTP/2 disable switch.

selectionNotes: Use only for a trusted Windows-auth service where HTTP/1.1 is permitted; keep strict HTTP/2 requests strict.

evidence.scope: Actual Windows x64 Kestrel HTTPS/HTTP2 with current Windows NTLM identity: paired manual and automatic authentication, strict HTTP2 and anonymous 401, public HTTP2, denied403 and wrong-name TLS rejection. No Kerberos/domain identity, proxy, other-platform, Linux security or final-GA proof.
